fatal_errors: The proposed material is a single-phase CoCrFeMnNi-type alloy, whereas the target system is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The intervention is high-strain-rate deformation rather than intermediate-temperature aging near 600-750 degrees C.
The claimed dynamic grain-boundary nanoclustering and cohesion-loss mechanism is not supported by either cited source.
The hypothesis misses the target structural mediators: enhanced L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
It does not predict the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile aging response, including minimum ductility near 600 degrees C and recovery near 750 degrees C.
explanation: The response is internally testable and proposes useful strain-rate controls, APT/TEM characterization, toughness measurements, and a clear falsification rule. It also recognizes conventional grain-boundary segregation and precipitation as competing explanations. However, it reconstructs neither the alloy, treatment, temperature window, microstructural mediator, mechanism, nor observed transition in the target study. E1 supports only generic grain-boundary embrittlement and thermally induced precipitation, while E2 concerns shear-induced grain refinement and dynamic surface softening; neither establishes deformation-induced Cr/Ni/Mn grain-boundary clustering, cavitation, or reduced cohesion. Thus the central mechanism is speculative rather than an evidence-supported alternative.
